title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC ruled both complaints administratively out of order for lack of standing and held that they could not be put in order. It did not decide the merits of either challenge.
first_summary: Turner challenged South Florida Presbytery Judicial Commission actions deposing TE Tommy Boland and dissolving Cross Community Church’s relationship with Presbytery. The SJC ruled both complaints administratively out of order for lack of standing because the congregation had already voted to disaffiliate. It treated the first withdrawal motion as immediately effective and the second, timing-related motion as out of order, concluding that no Presbytery action was required.
summary: Turner complained against Presbytery Judicial Commission actions deposing TE Tommy Boland and dissolving Cross Community Church’s relationship with Presbytery. The SJC ruled both complaints administratively out of order for lack of standing and incapable of being put in order. Cross Community had already disaffiliated through its first congregational motion; the second motion, which contemplated later implementation, was out of order as contingent. Because no Presbytery action was required to effect disaffiliation, Turner was no longer a PCA member. The underlying challenges were not decided.
